chapters.label: Player Account Roster
chapters.summary: The player account roster will support up to 12 characters and manage companions, main character swapping, and login. It integrates with existing grouping mechanics and is a core part of the ROMPE Sandbox plan, currently in the plan-only stage.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: A dozen character cards fanned out on a table, representing the account roster, with one card highlighted as the 'main' character and another slightly offset as the 'companion'.
chapters.currentState: The account roster is in a "plan-only" status, with no code yet implemented. It is identified as "S4 Account roster v0" of the ROMPE Sandbox. Open questions and architectural decisions are being documented.
chapters.intendedDesign: The design specifies an account supporting a roster of 12 characters, with one companion following the player's real character and other companions on a shared HUD. Players will be able to swap their main character at a Kafra and log in to the last main character played. The system will integrate with CommandGrants for owned bodies and manage player progression and an Account page hosted by the Binder.
chapters.nextSteps: The immediate next step is to begin implementation at phase "ACCOUNT-ROSTER.1a.1". This involves reading the current implementation tracker, the ROMPE Sandbox design section 9, groups design sections 0-4, and GROUPS-IMPL phases 1 and 2a, as well as relevant server code files.

chapters.label: Reworked Crafting Jobs
chapters.summary: The crafting system is being overhauled, turning the Blacksmith into a "forge" capable of Masterpiece quality items with an optional minigame, and the Alchemist into a "still" with a skill tree and brewing. This replaces older Episode 8 crafting designs.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: A blacksmith's forge glowing with heat, surrounded by tools and various raw materials. Nearby, an alchemist's still bubbles with colorful concoctions, surrounded by intricate diagrams and ingredient vials.
chapters.currentState: The reworked crafting jobs are currently in a "plan-only" status, encompassing slices S5 and S10 of the ROMPE Sandbox build order. Existing server-side item effects for Mini Furnace and hammers are inert. Weapon Repair is blocked pending the completion of RISK-ZONES.4b.
chapters.intendedDesign: The Blacksmith role will become a 'forge', allowing for crafting items up to Masterpiece quality, including an optional minigame. The Alchemist will become a 'still' with a real skill tree and brewing mechanics. Tempering operations will be available anywhere through the Crafting Book, without requiring tool items. Ore Discovery will credit players with loot priority, and crafting success will not spend materials if focus or material pools are insufficient, resulting in 0% return.
chapters.nextSteps: Unknown — not established by the captured evidence.

> Living design+status doc for **the reworked crafting jobs**. The Blacksmith becomes the forge: quality up to
> Masterpiece, the account crafter door and an optional forge minigame. The Alchemist becomes the still: a real skill tree

  holder of the skill, anywhere. Mini Furnace and the hammers stay inert (`Script/Items/ItemEffects.txt:93-96`).

  (vanilla). The ORO effect (extra Surge yield) waits for the Surge layer (rompe-sandbox §12.4, not built).

  the player word stays "forge". Window ids equal quest ids: `forge-smith` and `forge-still`.
- **D13 — mod channel only.** No `PacketType` or `AdminAction` change. Door actions ride CRAFTING's `crafting-book`
  window verb. The minigame rides the `quest-platform` channel with optional extra fields.

chapters.label: Crafting Book v0
chapters.summary: Crafting Book v0, part of the ROMPE Sandbox, features unlocked recipes, a Material Atlas, Kafra workshops for crafting, and salvage. It tracks player 'Want' for recipes and integrates with Ledger and other core systems, currently in "plan-only" status.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: An open, elaborately bound book displaying numerous crafting recipes. Beside it, a bustling Kafra workshop with various materials and tools, and a pile of discarded items ready for salvage.
chapters.currentState: Crafting Book v0 is in a "plan-only" status, covering slices S1-S2 of the ROMPE Sandbox core plan. All recipes are unlocked. The system integrates with SANDBOX-DATA, LEDGER, KAFRA-LINK, FIRST-15, CRAFT-JOBS, KAFRA-BOARD, SANDBOX-OPS, RISK-ZONES, and KAFRA-HIRE. There is no existing crafting documentation in the `reference/` or `impl/` directories.
chapters.intendedDesign: The Crafting Book v0 will allow players to turn a desired recipe (a "Want") into a Ledger Errand. A Material Atlas will inform players where to find materials. The Kafra workshop will serve as the first of three crafting doors, offering Normal quality crafting for a fee. The system will also include a salvage mechanic that returns a share of materials.

chapters.summary: The 'FIRST-15' system is designed to guide new characters through their initial 15 minutes, starting in a living field outside their town. It provides essential items, a borrowed companion, and aims for job level 10 quickly, built as a hidden ambient map mode.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: A newly spawned character stands in a vibrant, grassy field, a Poporing monster nearby. A friendly, high-level companion materializes beside them, ready for adventure.
chapters.currentState: FIRST-15 is in a "plan-only" status as of 2026-10-21, part of slice S1 of the ROMPE Sandbox core plan. It is intended to be a hidden ambient map mode with a per-character run. The starter field for new characters defaults to prt_fild08 for Prontera and Izlude, with other start towns disabled until their specific tests and recipe checks pass. This retains the Classic Return D18 design of starting in a random classic town.
chapters.intendedDesign: New characters will be born in a living field outside their start town, equipped with a Poporing with a knife, three First Aid kits, a "Want," a craft, and a borrowed level-80 companion, aiming to reach job level 10 around minute 12. The player's save point will be determined by the chosen start town, using `StartCityCatalog.PickSavePoint`.

## Open Questions

> Spec Kit-style clarify step. ≤3 items, auto-resolved with Rule 13 defaults on 2026-10-21. The operator can override
> any of them before the owning phase starts.

1. **Q:** Which field is the starter field, and whose save point does a new character get?
   **Resolution:** Keep Classic Return D18 ("start in a random classic town", `design/classic-return.md:625`, `:815`).

   > reference: the gate warps run both ways (`Script/Warps/Towns/Prontera.txt:12`, `Script/Warps/Fields/PronteraFields.txt:52`),
   > Kafra Sorin stands at the south gate (`Script/Npcs/Kafra.txt:481`), the fauna is level 1–6 with Jellopy at 70–75%
   > (`Db/DropData.csv:209`, `:70`), and path bots already hunt it (PPB run 4). Izlude also warps onto it

chapters.label: Caravan Event Layer
chapters.summary: The Caravan layer is a planned scheduled event where Kafra Corp wagons travel between cities, guarded by escorts and attacked by raiders. It's a core component of the ROMPE Sandbox, integrating risk zones and group mechanics.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: A robust Kafra Corp wagon, pulled by Peco Pecos, rolls along a dusty road between two distant cities. Armed escorts flank it, while shadowy figures lurk in the surrounding wilderness, poised to raid.
chapters.currentState: The Caravan event layer is in a "plan-only" status as of 2026-10-21, designated as Slice S6 Caravan v0. It is defined as a scheduled event where a Kafra Corp wagon travels between cities. The wagon itself is implemented as a monster objective (`CARAVAN_WAGON` 7020) with `AiEmpty`, no EXP, and no drops, spawned and managed by a `CaravanArena`.
chapters.intendedDesign: The Caravan event will involve player escorts guarding the wagon and raiders attempting to break it. Consigned goods will be transported within the wagon. The route's risk color (blue, yellow, red, black) will influence who can join the raid side, a pay multiplier, and the spill mechanic. PvP gates on red and black maps will allow player interaction with escorts, while sealed matches will override this.

chapters.label: Sky & Time of Day System
chapters.summary: A P0 in-progress day/night cycle system for ROMPE. It visually changes over time based on server or local time, driven by visual data, not code. It uses 32-bit pixel art for sky and light, with enclosed maps having no cycle.
chapters.detail: Read the captured evidence below. Source documents may describe plans rather than implemented behavior.
chapters.visual: A dynamic pixel-art sky gradually shifts from a vibrant morning orange to a deep twilight blue, casting changing light over a classic Ragnarok landscape. Stars begin to twinkle, and a crescent moon rises.
chapters.currentState: The sky and time of day system is P0 in progress. Currently, no sky is rendered; the `Default-Skybox` is unused in 232 scenes, and `IGfxService.SetSkybox` has no callers. There are no sky/star/moon shaders or sprites. The existing default skyboxes use the built-in procedural sky.
chapters.intendedDesign: The system will feature a day/night cycle as a live visual layer, driven by either server time or local time, with administrative controls to switch it off or pin it to a specific hour. Day and night behavior will be map-group specific visual data. The sky will be rendered as good-looking 32-bit pixel art, compatible with the lighting. Enclosed maps (dungeons, interiors) will have no cycle and a fixed sky setting. The system aims for performant rendering on WebGPU.
chapters.nextSteps: The immediate next step is for the tracker (SKY-TIME-IMPL.md) to be updated, especially for the P0 in-progress items, and to resolve the "sun in every cave" lesson into rule 3 in section 3 of the design.

# Sky & Time of Day — Design

> **Operator direction, 2026-10-18.** A day/night cycle built *on* the visual layer system: a live layer that
> changes over time, visible in the Visual tab overriding the config values it touches, driven by server time or
> local time, which an admin can switch off or pin to a specific hour. How day and night behave per map group is
> visual data, not code. TPS/FPS look at the sky, so the sky must be good-looking 32-bit pixel art that works with
> the light. Enclosed maps (dungeons, interiors) get no cycle and a proper sky setting. Design only; performant on
> WebGPU.
> Status: **P0 in progress** (2026-10-19). §12 answered by the operator 2026-10-19. Tracker:
> [../SKY-TIME-IMPL.md](../SKY-TIME-IMPL.md).
> Grounding: a read-only sweep of the client, server and docs on 2026-10-18. "Today" claims carry a file reference
> (C = `RebuildClient/Assets/Scripts`); line numbers drift.
> Related: [../research/oro-look-system.md](../research/oro-look-system.md) (the capability/values rule this follows),
> [../reference/visual-layers.md](../reference/visual-layers.md), [../reference/map-tags.md](../reference/map-tags.md),
> backlog item **CAMVIEW-SKY** (`docs/BACKLOG.md:313`), which this design closes.
